identity.name: Automated Linux Privilege Escalation via Staged Traitor Binary
identity.summary: Automated Linux Privilege Escalation via Staged Traitor Binary — the tool is DEPLOYED WITH PAYLOAD (digest-pinned, staged to /tmp/traitor-amd64 via the payload shelf, wired by adapter_ref TOOL-TRAITOR).
identity.description: A service account stages and runs traitor-amd64 from /tmp/traitor-amd64 — delivered through the Cortex POV payload shelf (sha256-pinned fdfbfc07248c3359…, adapter TOOL-TRAITOR) rather than an inline internet download, so the attack survives the customer's default-deny egress and the absent detection is never a manufactured false negative. Cortex should detect the execution of this tool from a writable path and its file hash.

execution.framework_reference_id: T1082 — automated Linux privilege-escalation enumeration (LinPEAS / pspy / SUID3NUM) executed by a web-server service account from a staging directory.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR Linux agent installed and reporting on the target endpoint.
prerequisites.check_command: systemctl is-active cortex-agent || ps aux | grep -i cortex

prerequisites.description: The payload shelf carries linpeas.sh, pspy64 and suid3num.py, pinned to the digests in tools/packs/{linpeas,pspy,suid3num}.yml. Verify BEFORE the customer is watching.
An enrolled beacon whose capabilities include artifact fetch (pull mode), or a generated bash bundle on a target that DOES have public-internet egress (push mode).

A POSIX target with `python3` on PATH and a LOGIN-CAPABLE www-data account. Both were found missing on a bare ubuntu:22.04 during the 2026-08-05 beacon proof: no python3 made step-04 exit 127, and www-data's /usr/sbin/nologin shell made `runuser -l www-data` refuse before any step ran. Both fail LOUDLY, which is correct — but a DC should discover them here, not in front of a customer.
prerequisites.check_command: command -v python3 && getent passwd www-data | grep -qv nologin

payload.code:
# MATURE: the tool is deployed WITH the payload via the digest-pinned payload shelf.
# SimCore stages traitor-amd64 to /tmp/traitor-amd64 (sha256 fdfbfc07248c3359…); this payload only runs it.
set -euo pipefail
[ -s /tmp/traitor-amd64 ] || { echo '[FATAL] PAYLOAD_NOT_STAGED_ON_TARGET:/tmp/traitor-amd64 — the TTP did NOT run; absent detections are NOT a Cortex miss' >&2; exit 1; }
sha256sum /tmp/traitor-amd64
/tmp/traitor-amd64 -a   # enumerate + auto-exploit a local misconfiguration to root (lab only)

expected_artifacts.description: The staged tool traitor-amd64 executed from a writable path by a service account.
The digest-pinned traitor-amd64 staged on the target.

iocs.context: Digest-pinned traitor-amd64 delivered via the payload shelf; benign tool, malicious-in-context when run from /tmp/traitor-amd64 by a service account.

biocs.name: Payload-Shelf Tool traitor-amd64 Executed From a Writable Path by a Service Account
biocs.description: A non-root service account executes traitor-amd64 from /tmp/traitor-amd64 — a privilege-escalation/container-breakout tool staged into a writable path, distinct from normal admin tooling.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_path contains "/tmp/traitor-amd64" or action_process_image_path contains "/tmp/traitor-amd64"
| filter actor_effective_username != "root"
| comp count() as execs by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_image_path
| filter execs >= 1

xql_queries.query:

| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START

abiocs.name: First-Seen Execution of a Privesc/Escape Tool From /tmp on This Host
abiocs.description: A host that has never run traitor-amd64 suddenly executes it from a writable path moments after the file is staged — the stage→chmod→exec chain of a deployed offensive tool.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("sh","bash") and action_process_image_path contains "traitor-amd64"
| comp count() as first_runs by agent_hostname, action_process_image_path
abiocs.causality_anchor: payload-shelf file-write of /tmp/traitor-amd64 -> chmod +x -> first execution of traitor-amd64 by a service-account shell

products.evidence_query: preset = xdr_data | filter actor_effective_username in ("www-data", "apache", "nginx") | filter action_process_image_path contains_any ("/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "/dev/shm/") | fields _time, agent_hostname, causality_id, action_process_image_command_line
preset = xdr_data | filter causality_actor_process_image_name = "apache2" | comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as chain_breadth by causality_id | filter chain_breadth >= 6

threat_scenarios.name: Shelf-Staged Privilege-Escalation Enumeration
threat_scenarios.description: Detect automated Linux privilege-escalation enumeration run by a web-server service account from a staging directory, and stitch the stages back to the web server as causality group owner.

threat_steps.objective: The BEHAVIOURAL detections fire on the canonical run.
preconditions: BIOCs from this card imported and enabled.
The payload shelf resolves SIM-EDR-022 with air_gapped = true.
steps: Compose and launch SIM-EDR-022 in pull mode against an enrolled beacon.
Read the Cortex console for the seven behavioural BIOCs.
success_criteria: BIOC `EDR-022 Service Account Spawns Interpreter Under Web Server CGO` fires within 60s.
BIOC `EDR-022 Automated Discovery Binary Breadth Burst` fires with discovery_breadth >= 6.
BIOC `EDR-022 Filesystem Wide Suid Sgid Sweep By Service Account` fires.
All three XQL validation queries return >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: The chain stitches to the web-server causality owner (TC-EDR-05).
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-EDR-0022` groups the stages from one causality_id into one incident.
The Causality View root is apache2 under www-data, NOT cortexsim-agent.
Process, file and network artifacts are present and temporally ordered.

threat_steps.objective: RENAME NEGATIVE CONTROL — behavioural coverage is proven independent of the tool name.
preconditions: The scenario-loader track has landed external_tools[].stage_as (S-19/S-20), OR the run is composed with a POST /api/shelf/compose stage_as override.
steps: Diff which detections fired against the canonical run.
success_criteria: The seven behavioural BIOCs STILL fire.
`EDR-022 Filename Keyed Linpeas Command Line Negative Control` and the filename IOCs do NOT fire.
The sha256 IOC still fires — a rename changes the destination, never the bytes.
If the behavioural BIOCs also darken, the reported finding is that the customer's endpoint coverage is name-keyed, NOT that the TTP failed to run.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Authored the payload-shelf EDR card: seven BEHAVIOURAL BIOCs (service-account interpreter spawn under a web-server CGO, discovery-binary breadth burst, privesc read fan-out, staging-directory execution, /proc cmdline sweep, cron-path read, SUID sweep, interpreter-on-staged-script) plus two deliberately filename-keyed detections and two filename IOCs labelled NEGATIVE-CONTROL TARGET, and three sha256 IOCs pinned to the adapter packs' install.artifact digests. Correlation CR-EDR-0022 stitches the chain to the apache2 causality owner for TC-EDR-05. Promoted to active.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Verified end-to-end against a real enrolled beacon (5/5 steps green under www-data, run status complete, tooling served from the SimCore shelf and sha256-verified against the composition's carried-in digests). Two real prerequisites surfaced by that run and recorded: python3 on PATH (absent on bare ubuntu:22.04 -> step-04 exit 127) and a login-capable www-data shell (nologin -> runuser refuses before any step runs). step-03 now enumerates 0 and 124 as success rather than using `|| true`, so 126/127 from a missing staged artifact still fail the run.

preventive_controls: Mount /tmp, /var/tmp and /dev/shm noexec on servers so a staged script cannot be executed at all.
Run the web tier under a shell-less account (/usr/sbin/nologin) so an interpreter spawn is impossible, not merely visible.
Restrict egress from application servers so an un-staged enumerator cannot fetch itself.
Remove unnecessary SUID/SGID bits and audit the remaining set on a schedule.
detection_engineering: Alert on ANY interpreter spawn whose causality owner is a web server — the highest-signal, lowest-volume rule on this card.
Prefer breadth and fan-out aggregations over tool-name string matches: rename-resistant by construction.
Keep filename rules, but score them as corroboration only, and periodically run a rename control to prove the behavioural rules carry the detection on their own.
Hash IOCs survive a rename; filename IOCs do not. Track which of the two your coverage actually rests on.
